question: Consider $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ defined by $f(n)=2n+1$. Determine whether $f$ is onto. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Testing an element of the co-domain
For $f$ to be onto, every element of $\mathbb{N}$ must be the image of some $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Consider $2\in\mathbb{N}$.

Pre-image condition
If $f(n)=2$, then
$$2n+1=2.$$
Therefore,
$$n=\frac{1}{2}.$$
But $\frac{1}{2}\notin\mathbb{N}$.

Conclusion
Thus, $2$ has no pre-image in $\mathbb{N}$. Therefore, $f$ is not onto.

options.B: $f$ is onto because every $m\in\mathbb{N}$ has the pre-image $n=\frac{m-1}{2}$ in $\mathbb{N}$
options.C: $f$ is not onto because $2$ has no pre-image in $\mathbb{N}$
options.D: $f$ is not onto because $3$ has no pre-image in $\mathbb{N}$
